claim: Human capital can be projected as a multi-state population: people are cross-classified by age, sex and education level and cohorts flow through education transitions.
model_or_dataset: Wittgenstein Centre multi-state cohort-component model (120-country run)
method: Multi-state cohort-component. Education is an explicit state; education-specific fertility, mortality and migration; 5-year projection steps; education progression assumptions in section 4.5.
outputs: Population by 5-year age group, sex and 4 education levels, 2005-2050, 120 countries (93% of 2005 world population); four scenarios (constant enrolment numbers CEN, constant enrolment ratio CER, global education trend GET, fast-track FT).
reusability: Reusable method: equations and scenario definitions are published; the input data must be rebuilt or sourced.
source_authors: Samir KC; Bilal Barakat; Anne Goujon; Vegard Skirbekk; Warren Sanderson; Wolfgang Lutz
source_title: Projection of populations by level of educational attainment, age, and sex for 120 countries for 2005-2050
notes: Full text read (92 pp). Open access CC BY-NC 2.0 DE, so figures/equations may be reused with attribution. This is the single clearest methodological template in the strand: it shows exactly how to run education as a state in a cohort-component engine.

claim: The full Wittgenstein Centre system covers 195 countries to 2100 and documents every data assumption and scenario.
model_or_dataset: Wittgenstein Centre (WIC) population projections by age, sex and level of education
method: Multi-state cohort-component; assumptions for fertility, mortality and migration derived from structured expert judgement combined with statistical models, then translated into education-specific trajectories.
outputs: Population by age, sex and six ISCED-1997-based education categories for 195 countries to 2100 (171 with education data, 24 expanded).
reusability: Citable methodology document; fully reimplementable in principle.
source_authors: Samir K.C.; Michaela Potancokova; Ramon Bauer; Anne Goujon; Erich Striessnig (approved by Wolfgang Lutz)
source_title: Summary of Data, Assumptions and Methods for New Wittgenstein Centre for Demography and Global Human Capital (WIC) Population Projections by Age, Sex and Level of Education for 195 Countries to 2100
notes: Full text read (87 pp). Six education categories with ISCED mapping rules (section 2), education assumptions section 3.5, education scenarios 4.7, education-specific migration 4.8. Cite this, not the book, for method statements.

claim: A 2018 update projects 201 countries under SSP-consistent scenarios and adds labour-force participation for EU member states.
method: Multi-state cohort component with SSP narratives; labour-force participation module for EU countries.
outputs: Population and human capital by age, sex and education for 201 countries to 2100; labour-force participation for EU members.
reusability: Citable; report distributed free by the Publications Office of the EU.
source_authors: Wolfgang Lutz; Anne Goujon; Samir KC; Marcin Stonawski; Nikolaos Stilianakis (eds)
source_title: Demographic and Human Capital Scenarios for the 21st Century: 2018 assessment for 201 countries
venue: Publications Office of the European Union (JRC), Luxembourg
notes: WU Vienna record opened and abstract read (ISBN 978-92-79-78024-0, publisher, DOI confirmed). The PDF itself returned a WU landing page and the EU Publications Office returned HTTP 403, so no table was read. Do not quote a number from this report until the PDF is obtained.

claim: The 2023 WIC update is openly licensed and downloadable, so its numbers can be reused directly rather than rebuilt.
model_or_dataset: WIC Population and Human Capital Projections - 2023 (dataset behind WCDE 3.0)
method: Multi-state cohort-component, 2020 base, SSP-consistent; the served vintage is WIC3.005.
outputs: Population by age, sex and education, plus reconstructions 1950-2020, for all countries; the base of the mean-years-of-schooling and attainment-distribution series in the Data Explorer.
reusability: Directly reusable. CC BY 4.0, so attribution-only reuse is permitted.
source_authors: Samir KC; Moradhvaj; Michaela Potancokova; Saroja Adhikari; Dilek Yildiz; Maria Mamolo; Tomas Sobotka; Krystof Zeman; Guy Abel; Wolfgang Lutz; Anne Goujon
source_title: Wittgenstein Center (WIC) Population and Human Capital Projections - 2023
notes: Record page read: licence field is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; version WIC3.005, 11 authors, projection chain run 14-16 April 2025. This is the practical route to a reusable, citeable baseline for a synthetic workbench.

claim: A public web data explorer exposes the WIC reconstructions and projections interactively and allows download.
model_or_dataset: Wittgenstein Centre Human Capital Data Explorer (WCDE) 3.0
method: Web front end over the WIC projections and reconstructions; CSV download of selected indicators.
outputs: Population size, education distribution, mean years of schooling (by age and broad age), dependency ratios, gender gaps, by country/sex/year.
reusability: Reusable as a data source and as an external benchmark for generated series.
source_title: Wittgenstein Centre Human Capital Data Explorer 3.0
notes: Page read; free, no registration. The page states the explorer serves the 2023 update 'published in K.C. et al. (2024)'. Good for checking a generator's mean-years-of-schooling output against an external series.

claim: The WIC projections are the human-capital core of the IPCC Shared Socioeconomic Pathways, so they connect a schooling model to a policy-standard baseline.
model_or_dataset: SSP population and human-capital scenarios (human core)
method: Multi-state cohort component applied to five SSP narratives.
outputs: Population by age, sex and education 2010-2100 for all countries, by SSP.
source_title: The human core of the shared socioeconomic pathways: Population scenarios by age, sex and level of education for all countries to 2100
notes: Metadata verified via OpenAlex (volume 42, pp. 181-192). Elsevier full text not retrieved. Use C01/C02 for method quotations and cite this for the SSP linkage only.

claim: The canonical book-length statement of the WIC approach exists and is the standard citation for the whole programme.
model_or_dataset: World Population and Human Capital in the Twenty-First Century (edited volume)
method: Edited volume; multi-state cohort-component chapters plus country/region chapters.
outputs: Global population and human capital by age, sex and education to 2100; scenario results and country narratives.
reusability: Citable as a book; not machine-reusable.
source_authors: Wolfgang Lutz; William P. Butz; Samir KC (eds)
source_title: World Population and Human Capital in the Twenty-First Century
notes: Metadata verified via OpenAlex (OUP eBooks, 2014). The OUP product page returned a JavaScript challenge (HTTP 202, 2 KB), so no chapter was read. Cite for the approach and the headline result, never for a specific number.

claim: Educational attainment for 1950-2010 can be reconstructed for a large country panel, but the method is extrapolation and back-casting, not projection.
method: Reconstruction: census/survey observations extrapolated forward and backward by 5-year age group at 5-year intervals; enrolment-adjustment for ages 15-24; education-specific survival for ages 65+; completion ratios to split complete/incomplete levels. Assumes attainment is fixed from age 25 to 64 and mortality is uniform across education.
outputs: Attainment shares by 5-year age group and sex, four broad levels split into complete/incomplete, 1950-2010, for the country panel; 15+ and 25+ series.
reusability: Reusable data; method citable. No forward projection is published by the authors.
source_title: A new data set of educational attainment in the world, 1950-2010
notes: The methodology page was read in full at barrolee.com and states the extrapolation procedure verbatim; the site's own citation gives JDE vol. 104, pp. 184-198, 2013 (OpenAlex lists online-first 2012). Important: Barro-Lee is a RECONSTRUCTION, not a projection - there is no forward-projection product on the site. Any projection 'built on Barro-Lee' must be sought elsewhere (the WIC series, C01-C04, is the comparable lineage).

claim: The Barro-Lee data are publicly downloadable and can be used to cross-check base-year attainment in a synthetic workbench.
method: Reconstruction/extrapolation (see C08); 5-year age groups; 15+ and 25+ series; 2021 update extends coverage to 1950-2015 for ages 15-64.
outputs: Country x 5-year age x sex x education shares; long-run enrolment ratios; a separate educational-quality/test-score dataset.
reusability: Reusable (free download from the project site).
notes: Site read. The site asks to be cited as Barro & Lee 2013 JDE 104:184-198. No explicit licence statement was seen on the pages read - verify terms before redistributing. Useful mainly as an independent check on base-year attainment shares, not as a projection engine.

claim: A ministry can simulate cohort flows and the cost of hitting enrolment targets in a generic model, with the financing gap as the output.
model_or_dataset: EPSSim 2.1 (Education Policy and Strategy Simulation Model)
method: 'Demographic' simulation: school-age population -> first-grade intake -> intake rate, enrolment ratios and flow rates -> enrolments by level -> teachers, classrooms, materials -> recurrent and investment expenditure against macro/budget indicators. Enrolment targets are the independent variables; expenditure is the consequence.
outputs: Projected intake, enrolment and flow rates; graduates; teacher and personnel needs; classrooms and materials; recurrent and investment expenditure; budget gap; by year and scenario.
reusability: Reusable tool and method: UNESCO distributes it free; the guide is a full specification.
source_title: Education Policy & Strategy Simulation Model (EPSSim) Version 2.1 User's Guide
venue: UNESCO, Education Policies and Strategies series
notes: Full text read (52 pp). States that the model is generic and needs country adaptation, and warns it is not sufficient for a detailed action plan. This is the closest existing 'national education sector simulation model' and the best structural precedent for a cost-and-flow workbench.

claim: UNESCO set out a generic computer-simulation model for education planning that countries could adapt themselves.
model_or_dataset: UNESCO generic education planning simulation model
method: Cohort/flow simulation plus cost and finance model; three scenario modes (extrapolation, exploration, forecasting).
outputs: Projections of enrolment flows, teacher requirements, physical inputs and costs; worked sample projections in the annexes.
reusability: Citable; the report explicitly invites reproduction with acknowledgement.
notes: Full text read (85 pp). Copyright page: 'Any part of this paper may be freely reproduced with the appropriate acknowledgement.' This is the conceptual parent of EPSSim and the best single citation for 'cohort-flow + cost simulation' as a planning method.

claim: The World Bank's standard policy toolkit embeds a computerised education-sector simulation model used in ministry planning.
model_or_dataset: Tools for Education Policy Analysis (book + CD-ROM)
method: Simulation model embedded in a broader policy-analysis toolkit (sector diagnosis, cohort flow, costs).
outputs: Sector projections and policy simulations (exact outputs not verified this session).
reusability: Citable precedent; not verified for method detail.
source_authors: Alain Mingat; Jee-Peng Tan; Shobhana Sosale
notes: DOI and imprint verified via OpenAlex and the DOI resolver; the OKR entity page is a JavaScript shell (2.3 KB) and the book itself was not read. Do NOT describe its equations until read. Included because it is the World Bank counterpart to EPSSim that a ministry-facing precedent section would be expected to cite.

claim: A dynamic microsimulation can carry each individual through schooling choices and generate attainment and labour-supply projections.
method: Dynamic microsimulation: individual life courses through start / level-and-field choice / completion / continuation, plus a module that updates attainment without enrolment; transition probabilities estimated on Norwegian register data 1999-2009; embedded in a demographic projection engine.
outputs: Population by educational background; labour supply by education; long-run public expenditure.
reusability: Precedent only: register-based, national, and not portable without population registers.
source_title: Educational behavior in the dynamic micro-simulation model MOSART
notes: Full text read (58 pp; ISBN 978-82-537-8628-5). The closest microsimulation precedent for individual-level schooling transitions, and a useful contrast: it needs linked registers, which is exactly the data a synthetic workbench would have to invent.

claim: Agent-based models have been used to model schooling transitions and district-level outcomes emerging from household decisions.
model_or_dataset: Agent-based model of the transition to public school choice (Chicago)
method: Agent-based: household school choice with achievement/Proximity preferences, school admission and capacity dynamics; initialised on Chicago Public Schools data.
outputs: District achievement distribution, sorting and segregation patterns; effect of the number and timing of new school entry.
reusability: Precedent for ABM style and validation, not for attainment projection.
source_authors: Spiro Maroulis; Eytan Bakshy; Louis Gomez; Uri Wilensky
source_title: Modeling the Transition to Public School Choice
venue: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation 17(2):3
notes: Full text read (14 pp). Models choice and sorting, not cohort attainment, so it is a docking/validation precedent rather than a projection model. Useful as evidence that education ABMs are publishable in a methods journal.

claim: UIS has published global teacher-demand projections derived from a cohort-flow model, which would be the UN statistical office's own projection product.
method: Pupil-teacher-ratio and flow model (details not verified).
outputs: Projected teacher numbers required to reach universal primary education by 2015, by region (details not verified).
reusability: Not usable until a live copy is retrieved.
source_authors: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (attributed to Michael Bruneforth in library records)
source_title: Projecting the global demand for teachers: meeting the goal of universal primary education by 2015
